points: Perek 52 was added later, after "these are the words of Yirmiyahu" closed the sefer.
Tzidkiyahu, who refused to surrender, tries to escape. He is caught; his sons are killed before him and he is blinded.
Pesukim 12–26 detail the destruction of Yerushalayim and the looting of its treasures; then the count of exiles.
The sefer ends with Yehoyachin, who surrendered, freed after 37 years in jail and given a seat above the other kings: a small note of hope.
